title: A locally quasi-finite morphism is locally of finite type (Stacks, remark after 01TD)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]: every $x\in X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A=U\subseteq X$ and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] such that the ring map $R=\mathcal O_S(V)\to A=\mathcal O_X(U)$ induced by $f$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and quasi-finite at the prime of $A$ corresponding to $x$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Morphisms, Section Tag 01TC (section-quasi-finite), remark after Definition Tag 01TD, line 3558 ('Trivially, a locally quasi-finite morphism is locally of finite type'); the locality of finite type it rests on is Lemma Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), line 2673

proof.text: *Each point has a finite type affine pair.* Let $x\in X$. By [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2), $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$, so by [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1) there are an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $x\in U$ and an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ such that the ring map $R=\mathcal O_S(V)\to A=\mathcal O_X(U)$ induced by $f$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] (and quasi-finite at the prime of $x$, which is not used below). Hence every $x\in X$ lies in an affine open $U$ mapped by $f$ into an affine open $V$ with $\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ of finite type.

source.place: Morphisms, remark after Definition Tag 01TD (definition-quasi-finite, line 3538), line 3558 ('Trivially, a locally quasi-finite morphism is locally of finite type')

proof.text: *Conclusion.* The condition obtained in step 1 for every $x\in X$ is exactly the right-hand side of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] (Stacks Definition 01T1 with Lemma 01T2, (1) $\Leftrightarrow$ (2) $\Leftrightarrow$ (4)); by its implication from right to left, $f$ is locally of finite type in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

split_report.summary: Two steps following the remark after Stacks 01TD ('Trivially...'): unpack pqf-def-quasifinite (1)-(2) to get, around every point, an affine pair with a finite type ring map (the quasi-finiteness is dropped); then the pointwise criterion for local finite type. In Stacks this criterion is the definition 01T1; in the DAG locally of finite type is the affine-cover form of def-weil-finite-type-morphism, so the agreement (01T1 with 01T2) is cited as the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion = HasRingHomProperty.iff_exists_appLE for LocallyOfFiniteType / RingHom.FiniteType (RingHomProperties.lean:651, read). The existing lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs (all affine pairs, 01T2 (1)<=>(2)) does not give the pointwise direction. Statement kept; stmt_deps completed with def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime (notions the statement uses). Mathlib: no LocallyQuasiFinite => LocallyOfFiniteType (Mathlib's LocallyQuasiFinite omits finite type, QuasiFinite.lean:57), so the item is not a leaf.

reviewed: Reviewed by L 2026-10-10: 'trivially' in the source rests on Stacks' pointwise definition 01T1; the DAG's cover definition needs the pointwise criterion of 01T2, now a Mathlib leaf (HasRingHomProperty.iff_exists_appLE). Statement gained citations only. Not a leaf itself (Mathlib's LocallyQuasiFinite is a different notion, B8).
